request.system: You are a senior clinical coder in an Australian public hospital with fifteen years of experience coding inpatient episodes in ICD-10-AM. You are careful, conservative, and you never invent a code you are not sure of the chapter for.

messages.content:
Code the episode of care below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed. Give the three-character ICD-10-AM category for the principal diagnosis.

Hospital course:
HOSPITAL COURSE:

Admitted from the emergency room due to severe dyspnea, a 69-year-old Japanese man was diagnosed with aspiration pneumonia and placed on mechanical ventilation. He underwent tracheostomy due to prolonged mechanical ventilation and had restrictive pulmonary dysfunction. He was weaned successfully from mechanical ventilation with support by HFT (flow at 40 L/minute with FIO2 of 0.25) and a ventilator (10 cmH2O pressure support with 5 cmH2O PEEP) at night. The patient was discharged from the ICU to the general ward on ICU day 51. His physiotherapy rehabilitation continued for 1 month.
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES: [diagnosis section withheld]
TREATMENT:

Mechanical ventilation, tracheostomy, and respiratory support by HFT and a ventilator.

FOLLOW-UP AND RECOMMENDATIONS:

The patient was discharged to home on day 86 of hospitalization and returned for a follow-up visit. No further recommendations were provided.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The course describes admission for severe dyspnea, with a diagnosis of aspiration pneumonia that was then treated with mechanical ventilation. The diagnosis section is withheld, so the principal diagnosis has to come from the narrative. The only established condition that explains the admission is aspiration pneumonia.

In ICD-10-AM, aspiration pneumonia (pneumonitis due to inhalation of food or vomit) is classified to J69 (Pneumonitis due to solids and liquids), specifically J69.0. The restrictive pulmonary dysfunction is a later complication and not the reason for admission. Dyspnea is only a presenting symptom.

The underlying cause of the aspiration is not given, so I cannot code anything else as principal.

CODE: J69
